notes: Profiles that let Strays say which AI coding agent, terminal, or IDE started a process.

A process is attributed to an agent when (1) an ancestor in its parent chain matches ancestorMatchers, or (2) its environment contains one of envMarkers. An ancestor match wins over an environment match, and the nearest ancestor is checked first.
When only the environment matches, the process has been detached from the agent. If the agent session that started it is gone, Strays labels it 'Orphaned from <agent>'.

RULE FOR envMarkers: only list a variable you have seen yourself in the environment of a background process started through the agent, and say so in 'verified'. Variables that are merely believed to exist go in unverifiedEnvMarkers, which Strays never matches on.
To verify: start a long-running command through the agent, then run `strays inspect <pid>`. See CONTRIBUTING.md.

matchers: executableNames are exact basenames (case-sensitive); bundleNames are the outermost .app name; pathFragments are substrings of the executable path; argumentPatterns are regular expressions matched against the full command line.
To add or change profiles without rebuilding, put a file of the same shape at ~/Library/Application Support/Strays/agents.json. Entries with a matching id replace the built-in ones.

agents.notes: CLAUDE_PID holds the PID of the agent process that spawned the shell (verified 2026-10-12 on both versions: the CLI set it to its own PID, not the PID inherited from the session it was launched in). Strays uses it to tell a detached process whose session is still alive from a true orphan. The agent is a native binary these days (`claude`, or `claude.exe` inside the npm package); older releases ran `node …/@anthropic-ai/claude-code/cli.js`, which argumentPatterns still covers.
